data: North Korea's satellite launch site: Unha rockets (2012, 2016) and Chollima-1 (2023)

North Korea's main satellite launch site, also called Tongchang-ri, in Cholsan County, North Pyongan Province. The first launch from it was the failed Unha-3 flight of 13 April 2012 (07:39 Korea time); orbit was claimed on 12 December 2012 and 7 February 2016, and Chollima-1 reached orbit on 21 November 2023. Facts from Wikipedia (Sohae, Unha, Kwangmyongsong-3, Chollima-1); coordinates are the main pad (LP1) on Wikipedia.
After Hanoi Summit: Rebuilding of Sohae Launch Facility — CSIS Beyond Parallel

Sohae, also called Tongchang-ri, lies in hills near North Korea's border with China, in Cholsan County. Construction was visible in satellite images from the early 1990s and reported complete in 2011; the site covers over six square kilometres. The first launch was an Unha-3 rocket carrying Kwangmyongsong-3 on 13 April 2012; it failed shortly after liftoff. A second Unha-3 on 12 December 2012 placed an object in orbit, according to NORAD, and another Unha flew on 7 February 2016. A smaller, newer pad hosts Chollima-1: it failed on 30 May and 23 August 2023 (UTC), then put the Malligyong-1 reconnaissance satellite into orbit on 21 November 2023. The United States and others regard these launches as missile tests; parts of the site were dismantled in 2018 and rebuilt from 2019.
